description: For managing metrics of services dedicated to in-cluster deployment. If you use external components, such as RabbitMQ or ClickHouse, for correct filtering by cluster and if Grafana is configured for several clusters, add the "cluster" label to the metrics of these components (similar to other system metrics). You can also view information about the runtime monitor service connection to RabbitMQ.

panels.description:
Event processing time per detector.

If the duration is significantly higher than the average number, this may indicate an issue.
panels.title: Detector operating time

panels.description:
Duration of event processing by the entire detector chain.

Normally, the distribution should be around the middle of the hitmap. If the processing time is closer to the upper bound or regularly falls into +Inf, this may be a sign of an issue.
panels.title: Оperating time of the entire detector chain

panels.description:
The Runtime-Monitor service has an internal buffer for Tetragon events. It is designed to smooth out peaks in the load on the RabbitMQ queue provider.

If everything runs properly, in most cases, the size of this buffer will be around zero. If the size reaches the maximum value (1,000 by default), there may be an issue.
panels.title: Tetragon events buffer size

panels.description:
The Runtime-Monitor service has an internal buffer for Tetragon events. It is designed to smooth out peaks in the load on the RabbitMQ queue provider.

When the buffer is full, the following Tetragon messages will be lost. This metric shows the number of lost events.
panels.title: Tetragon events dropped count

panels.description: Threats found during event analysis by detectors in time.
panels.title: Threats found by the detector scan
Detector calls that ended in errors

panels.description:
The size of the event queue to be processed.

Events are processed by the Event-Processor service.
If the queue size grows, it means that Event-Processor cannot handle the load.

Check for errors in the logs and scale the Event-processor service accordingly.
panels.title: Queue size of events prepared for processing (Rabbit)
Rate of adding new events to rabbit
Failure rate when adding new events in Rabbit

panels.description:
The size of the queue of processed events to be sent.

Events are sent by the History-API service.
If the queue size grows, it means that the History-API cannot handle the load.

Check for errors in the logs and scale the History-API service accordingly.
panels.title: Queue size of history events after processing (Rabbit)
Rate of adding history events to rabbit
Failure rate when adding history events in Rabbit

panels.description: Distribution of the gRPS request processing time in a certain range of values.
panels.title: gRPC requests histogram

panels.description:
Processed events are sent to ClickHouse.

This graph shows the overall ClickHouse activity as well as the read and write speed.

If there is no activity, events are being processed and queued in RabbitMQ, or the speed is too low, this may indicate issues with the ClickHouse database.
panels.title: Clickhouse activity
